title: What If the Work Could Give You Energy Instead of Taking It Away?
introduction: You have the potential to discover what brings your abilities alive, see hidden connections, restore movement in difficult situations, and turn possibilities into reality. Function 7 is the energy of realization. It awakens when your interests, talents, and abilities find meaningful expression. Taking care of yourself, work, relationships, travel, dancing, learning, and creative ventures can become sources of vitality rather than obligations. When this function is fulfilled, curiosity, movement, inspiration, and purpose create momentum. Its strength is not rescuing others: it is seeing what remains viable, what needs to change, and how life can move again.

stories.title: The Monday Morning That Changed Everything
stories.narrative: It's Sunday evening. Tomorrow is Monday, and you already feel tired. Your work is respectable, and you're capable and responsible, yet every week feels like forcing yourself to move. Unexpectedly, someone asks you to untangle a complicated situation. As you listen, you see connections others have missed, recognize what matters, and sense a clear way forward. An hour passes unnoticed. For the first time in months, you feel energized. Why do you have endless energy for this, and so little for your ordinary days?

choices.choice: Dismiss the experience and return to what is familiar.
choices.outcome: You go back to routine. The spark fades, and you continue assuming tiredness is simply the price of responsibility.
choices.reflection: What valuable signal are you dismissing because it does not fit your current identity?

choices.choice: Chase the excitement without understanding what makes you feel alive.
choices.outcome: You rush into new activities. Some feel exciting briefly, but the energy scatters because you have not identified what truly engages your abilities.
choices.reflection: Which part of the experience energized you: novelty, recognition, discovery, or the work itself?

choices.choice: Recognize the talent being activated and explore how to make it part of your life.
choices.outcome: You notice your gift for seeing connections and restoring movement in stuck situations. You begin creating room for this ability in your work and life, testing where it produces genuine results. Monday starts to feel different.
choices.reflection: What kind of engagement activates your energy rather than consumes it?

stories.title: The Journey You Kept Postponing
stories.narrative: You have dreamed of visiting a distant place for years. Each time you think about going, obstacles appear: money, time, responsibilities, arrangements. One morning you realize you've spent more energy explaining why you cannot go than discovering how you could. You start looking at routes, seasons, possibilities, and the people who might help. The journey begins to feel real before you buy a ticket.

choices.choice: Put the dream aside until life becomes easier.
choices.outcome: You postpone again. The barriers stay vague and the destination becomes another story about what you might do someday.
choices.reflection: Which obstacle is real, and which has never been examined?

choices.choice: Book everything impulsively and hope it works out.
choices.outcome: The excitement carries you forward, but overlooked commitments create stress that diminishes the pleasure of the trip.
choices.reflection: How can you preserve spontaneity without ignoring what matters?

choices.choice: Find a workable route and begin with the first concrete step.
choices.outcome: You identify the essentials, adjust your timing and resources, and take one realistic step. The journey becomes a living possibility rather than an impossible wish.
choices.reflection: What dream could become real if you explored a different pathway?

stories.title: When Love Needs a New Way Forward
stories.narrative: Two people who once loved exploring life together now find that conversations end in frustration. They've explained, apologized, compromised, and promised to change. Nothing lasts. One evening, you wonder whether the issue is not a lack of love but a way of living together that no longer supports who you've become.

choices.choice: Repeat the same promises with greater determination.
choices.outcome: Both of you try harder for a while, but the underlying pattern remains. Disappointment returns.
choices.reflection: What has repeated despite your best intentions?

choices.choice: Try to make the other person change first.
choices.outcome: The conversation turns into a struggle over whose behavior is the problem. Curiosity disappears.
choices.reflection: What happens when understanding is replaced by control?

choices.choice: Explore a different approach that respects both people.
choices.outcome: You become curious about how each of you actually functions and what conditions support closeness. Small changes in rhythms, expectations, and shared experiences open a more honest possibility.
choices.reflection: What if the relationship doesn’t need another attempt to fulfill old promises, but would benefit from a different approach?

stories.title: The Company Everyone Thought Was Finished
stories.narrative: You are invited to examine a business close to closing. Revenue is falling, employees are exhausted, and the owner has tried cutting costs, hiring consultants, and introducing new systems. Everyone has a different explanation. As you listen, you begin to see how the problems connect. Several expensive activities no longer serve the company, while one overlooked capability still creates real value.

choices.outcome: The organization spreads its remaining energy across too many commitments. The most valuable capability receives too little attention.
choices.reflection: What are you preserving simply because it already exists?

choices.outcome: A new initiative consumes scarce resources without resolving the underlying tensions. People lose confidence.
choices.reflection: Does this solution simplify the situation or add another layer?

choices.choice: Identify the essential elements and develop a focused plan for rebuilding.
choices.outcome: You distinguish what still has life from what has run its course. With a few clear priorities, realistic resources, and evidence from early experiments, the company can test a new direction.
choices.reflection: What is still alive and valuable here—and what must be released to let it grow?
